brief: short pike/halberd with a copper fork head
biome: all (NPC accessory, attaches to installed humanoid cast)
author: Claude (coordinator-side Meshy NPC-accessory worker), owner-authorized Meshy use (Standing owner direction 1, 15 Oct 2026)
workflow: agent-drafted multi-view concept from the repo key art (Meshy image-to-image nano-banana-pro, reference as data URI) -> inspected -> Meshy image-to-3d (latest, quad remesh, target 2500, PBR textures embedded) -> Meshy remesh (triangle topology, target 3600) to meet the <4k-triangle budget -> embedded textures resized to 1024 px JPEG -> lossless metres normalisation -> origin moved to the attach point

native_size.note: Meshy remesh GLB, longest side ~1.9 units

scale_normalisation.method: lossless: GLB scene roots wrapped in node 'metres_root' with uniform scale + translation; base at y=0, footprint centred on x/z, then translation shifted so the attach point is the origin
scale_normalisation.source_glb: Meshy remesh output (triangle topology, target 3600) of the chosen image-to-3d model, textures re-encoded

texture_repack.method: every embedded image resized to <=1024 px and re-encoded JPEG q92 (Meshy remesh baked 2048-4096 px PNG)

origin.attach_point: grip on the shaft axis, 0.80 m up from the butt
origin.note: normalised frame = base at y=0, x/z centred; origin_offset is added to every vertex (glTF +y up, Meshy front faces +z)

previews: preview_meshy.png (Meshy thumbnail of the image-to-3d source model)
preview_3view.png (software flat-shaded 3-view of the final GLB, colours sampled per face)
files.raw_glb: not published (Meshy image-to-3d and remesh outputs kept only as task ids)

concepts.prompt: A short polearm pike: straight honey-brown wooden haft with leather grip wrap in the lower half and copper bands, topped by a two-prong copper fork head like a lightning rod with a small side blade, chunky and friendly rather than menacing. Style: Palworld / Animo-class stylised game asset, chunky simplified readable silhouette that reads at 15 metres, slightly oversized key shapes, soft hand-painted PBR materials, warm natural palette taken from the reference key art (honey wood, warm brass and copper, slate blue, teal, mustard, moss green, cream). Single isolated object only, floating on a plain flat light-grey background, no ground, no shadow scene, no character, no body, no hands, no mannequin, no text, no logo. Absolutely no red, no oxblood, no maroon, no crimson, no pink anywhere. Show the same object from three views: front, three-quarter and side, consistent design.
references: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MJohnsonWellabe/Tetherbound/main/docs/reference/tetherbound-meadows-keyart.png (1536 x 1024 source re-encoded as JPEG q90 at 1536 px; local derived file keyart_1536.jpg): project palette and stylised finish
concepts.verdict: CHOSEN (view 1, front-three-quarter): honey-wood haft with sage and cream grip wrap and copper bands, two-prong copper fork head with a brass collar and a small brass side blade; view 0 was edge-on

models.kept: source for remesh r1 only; raw GLB not published

visual_verdict.text: Friendly copper fork-pike: a big two-prong copper head (about 0.67 m across with the side blade) on a chunky honey haft (about 0.17 m across) with a sage and cream grip wrap. Readable at 15 m. Brief deviations: the head is large and flat (paddle-like prongs) and the haft is thick, so it reads more toy-like than a halberd. The copper is a light rose-copper (mean texel about 177/111/82 RGB); it is not red, but if judges read it as pink beside Team Tether oxblood, warm its tint toward orange at integration.

integration_note: candidate only; stays flag-off until its scene passes code-blind judging
palette_check: base-colour texture scan of the final GLB (hue <= 12 or >= 320 deg, sat >= 0.35, val >= 0.2): 0.56% of texels, all dark shaded copper/wood edge texels, no red/oxblood/pink surface
